entity.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
entity.description: Muhammad's cousin who split Islam into two branches. The fourth caliph and first Shia Imam, Ali married the Prophet's daughter Fatima and was renowned as the bravest warrior of early Islam. His assassination by a Kharijite dissident in 661 paved the way for the Umayyad dynasty and the permanent Sunni-Shia divide.

story.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
story.description: Possibly born inside the Ka'ba, serving as Muhammad's decoy during the hijra, winning the Battle of the Camel, then assassinated at prayer. The life that divided Islam forever.

moments.name: Ali Is Born in Mecca, Possibly Inside the Ka'ba Itself
moments.subtitle: The only person in Islamic tradition said to have been born inside Islam's holiest site
moments.description: Around 600 CE, Ali ibn Abi Talib was born in Mecca to Abu Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Fatima bint Asad. According to Islamic tradition, Ali may have been the only person born inside the Ka'ba, the holiest site in Islam. His father was a leading member of the Banu Hashim clan within the Quraysh tribe and had raised the orphaned Muhammad. When Abu Talib fell into poverty, the young Ali was taken in at about age five and raised in Muhammad's household. Aged about eleven, Ali became among the first to accept Muhammad's teachings and profess Islam.

moments.name: Ali Sleeps in Muhammad's Bed as a Decoy During an Assassination Plot
moments.subtitle: The young cousin risks his life so Muhammad can escape Mecca to Medina
moments.description: In 622 CE, when Muhammad learned of a plot to assassinate him, Ali stayed behind in Mecca as his decoy, sleeping in Muhammad's bed while the Prophet escaped to Yathrib (Medina). Ali risked his life knowing the assassins intended to kill whoever they found. This event marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar. According to Islamic tradition, Ali's willingness to sacrifice himself prompted the Quranic revelation about a man who gives his life to please God. Ali later escaped Mecca himself after returning goods that had been entrusted to Muhammad by Meccans.

moments.name: Ali Defeats a Rebel Army Led by Muhammad's Widow at the Battle of the Camel
moments.subtitle: The new caliph fights fellow Muslims for the first time in Islam's first civil war
moments.description: In 656 CE, Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib defeated a rebel force at the Battle of the Camel near Basra in Iraq. The rebels, led by Talha, Zubayr, and Muhammad's widow Aisha, had captured Basra to avenge the assassination of the previous caliph Uthman. The battle takes its name from the camel on which Aisha watched the fighting. Ali had been elected caliph in Medina after Uthman's murder in June 656, and this was the first major battle between Muslim factions. The conflict marked the beginning of Islam's first civil war (fitna), a rupture whose consequences still shape the Muslim world.

moments.name: Ali Fights Mu'awiya to a Standstill at the Battle of Siffin
moments.subtitle: A failed arbitration after the battle costs Ali supporters and creates the Kharijites
moments.description: In 657 CE, Caliph Ali fought the Syrian governor Mu'awiya at the Battle of Siffin along the Euphrates in present-day Syria. Mu'awiya, whom Ali had removed from the governorship of Syria, refused to accept Ali's authority and demanded vengeance for Uthman's murder. The battle ended inconclusively when Mu'awiya's troops raised Qurans on their lances, calling for arbitration. The resulting arbitration process failed and alienated a faction of Ali's supporters who became the Kharijites, a radical sect that rejected both leaders. This three-way split among Muslims would have fatal consequences for Ali himself.

moments.name: A Kharijite Assassin Strikes Ali with a Poisoned Sword at Morning Prayer
moments.subtitle: The fourth caliph's murder fractures Islam into Sunni and Shia branches forever
moments.description: In January 661 CE, the Kharijite dissident Ibn Muljam struck Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib with a poisoned sword while Ali was praying at the Great Mosque of Kufa in Iraq. Ali died from his wounds shortly after. His assassination cleared the path for Mu'awiya to seize power and establish the Umayyad Caliphate, ending the era of the Rashidun caliphs. Ali's shrine in nearby Najaf became one of the holiest sites in Shia Islam. Sunni Muslims regard Ali as the last rightly-guided caliph; Shia Muslims venerate him as the first Imam and Muhammad's rightful successor.
